YES

The script verifies key-set equality across all three checkpoints and bit-exact equality of every non-MLP tensor before touching anything, computes each task vector against the unmodified base in float32 with lambda 0.4, asserts exactly 48 merged and 160 output tensors, copies all other tensors from the base unchanged, and writes a single file to `out/T4/model.safetensors`. The only unread dependency is the local `_ckpt.load_checkpoint` helper, assumed to return a plain name-to-tensor dict.
